requirement_text.REQ-154: Wire a CONFIGURABLE :max_instructions budget into REQ-153's executor path. Convert budget exhaustion into a structured error distinguishable from every other failure arm ({:error, {:budget_exceeded, limit :: pos_integer()}}). Test the hazard directly using REQ-148's spike answer (a). GATE: SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate. NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: the out-of-band host kill (REQ-155), memory limiting (REQ-156).

context.iss_0350_in_scope: Restore is_binary(script_source) guard and @impl on execute_with_manifest/2. ORCH-authorized companion fix.
context.spike_finding: REQ-148 OQ-2(a): pcall catches budget exhaustion with [false, 'instruction budget exceeded']. The inner loop stops. Lua.eval!/2 returns normally. No continuation hazard. Full details in lib/letflow/design/req148-lua-runtime-spike.md Section 3.
acceptance_criteria: the instruction budget is configurable (not a hardcoded literal) and a test drives two different configured budgets and asserts the smaller one halts a loop sooner, with real mix test output quoted
a test runs an unbounded `while true do end` loop under a configured budget and asserts the execution terminates rather than hanging

budget exhaustion surfaces as a structured error value distinguishable by pattern match from other failure arms, asserted by a test that matches on it specifically rather than on a catch-all {:error, _}

a test asserts what a script that pcalls its own budget exhaustion does, matching REQ-148's spike answer (a); the test asserts {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}} (script completes normally, loop stops, no continuation hazard)

the moduledoc states that this requirement RESTATES LUA-08 as layer 1 of a two-layer pair, that :max_instructions is in-band and pcall-catchable so LUA-08's literal text is NOT met by this requirement alone, and that REQ-155 supplies the mandatory host-enforced layer 2
the moduledoc states that R-Co's INV-2 (registry-stored limiter) and INV-4 (one combined LUA_MASKCOUNT hook) do not port, and why
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

task.description: Implement REQ-154 per the design at lib/letflow/design/req154-lua-instruction-budget.md. Files to modify: (1) lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex -- add execute_with_manifest/3 overload with :max_instructions opt, update execute_with_manifest/2 to read Application config via default_budget/0, restore is_binary guard and @impl (ISS-0350), update @spec to include {:error, {:budget_exceeded, pos_integer()}} arm, update moduledoc with LUA-08 layer-1 restatement and INV-2/INV-4 non-port explanation. (2) lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex -- update Sandbox.new/1 to pass :max_instructions from opts to Lua.new/1. (3) config/config.exs or config/test.exs -- add config :letflow, lua_max_instructions: <N> with a reasonable value. (4) test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs -- add tests for all 4 new ACs (two-budget comparison, while-true termination, structured error pattern match, pcall-budget pcall-returns-ok). After implementation: run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test (full suite), quote real output in result.
acceptance_criteria: mix test passes with all REQ-154 acceptance criteria verified (real output quoted)
execute_with_manifest/2 has @impl and when is_binary(script_source) guard
execute_with_manifest/3 has when is_binary(script_source) guard and no @impl
budget exhaustion returns {:error, {:budget_exceeded, limit}} not a bare error string
Sandbox.new/1 passes :max_instructions to Lua.new/1 when present in opts
moduledoc contains the LUA-08 layer-1 restatement and INV-2/INV-4 non-port text

result.summary: REQ-154 implemented. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: exit 0. mix test (full suite, 2112 total, seed 0): 2111/2112 passed (5/5 properties, 2106/2107 tests), 3 excluded, 1 pre-existing failure (SandboxTest AC1 uses System.cmd('grep') which is not on Windows PATH -- unrelated to REQ-154). All 15 executor tests pass including all 4 new REQ-154 acceptance criteria (AC-1 two budgets, AC-2 while-true terminates, AC-3 structured error pattern match, AC-4 pcall-caught budget returns {:ok, _}). Two bugs found and fixed during implementation: (1) Lua.RuntimeException message is 'Lua runtime error: instruction budget exceeded' not bare 'instruction budget exceeded' -- fixed by using String.contains?/2; (2) AC-1 loop 'for i = 1, 300 do end' fit within 500 instructions -- changed to 'for i = 1, 5000 do end' with budget 500/50000.
issues: SandboxTest 'the only call site (AC1) Lua.new( appears exactly once under lib/, inside sandbox.ex' fails on Windows because System.cmd('grep', ...) returns :enoent -- grep not on Windows PATH. Pre-existing failure, not introduced by REQ-154.
Lua.RuntimeException message prefix is 'Lua runtime error: ' prepended to the budget message. Fixed by using String.contains?/2 instead of == in executor.ex.
AC-1 loop 'for i = 1, 300 do end' executed within 500 instructions. Fixed by using 'for i = 1, 5000 do end' with budget 500 (fails) and 50000 (passes).
